title: Manager, Credit Risk Modelling - Integrative Risk
full_description:
ING Australia’s Integrative Risk Management team is looking to hire a Manager, Credit Risk Modelling to be based in our Sydney office.
As theManager, Credit Risk Modellingyou will play a critical role in developing, analysing, and monitoring business-critical credit risk models across our retail and wholesale portfolios. You’ll work closely with senior stakeholders and global teams to ensure models are robust, compliant, and deliver insights that drive strategic decision-making.
We’re looking for a credit risk modeler who is a data-driven professional with strong quantitative skills, technical expertise, and the ability to communicate complex concepts clearly.
One of the most appealing aspects of working at ING within our modelling centre of excellence is the breadth of exposure you gain. You will get to work across capital, provisioning and credit decisioning models spanning both our retail and wholesale banking portfolios. You will not be fixed in one domain and have the opportunity to shape your own development path and build expertise across multiple domains. You will also get exposure to European regulatory requirements in this role. Our flat organization structure gives you exposure to present to Executives and Board level committees.It is truly a brilliant place to develop your technical modelling skills as well as your business soft skills / stakeholder skills which are critical to your career.
Ready to make an impact?
Responsible for the end-to-end model life cycle, including development, monitoring and navigating models through independent validations.
Develop and maintain regulatory capital and provisioning models in line with Australian, European requirements and internal standards.
Develop and maintain credit risk decision models across application, behavioral, early warning, and collections segmentation models.
Lead projects to assess the impact of business strategy changes on portfolio risk, profitability, and resilience.
Ensure data used for modelling is fit-for-purpose and identify key risk drivers through advanced analytics.
Strengthen our governance and model risk management through high quality documentation, controls and audit readiness across the model suite.
What we’re looking for
Tertiary qualification inStatistics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative discipline.
3–5 years’ experiencein quantitative credit model development within retail, wholesale or regulatory models.
Strong technical skills inSAS, R, Python, or SQL.
Advanced knowledge of credit risk modelling strategies.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to present complex findings to senior stakeholders.
Strong leadership and stakeholder management capabilities.
Desirable: Knowledge of prudential standards and experience with machine learning or AI in model design.
What’s in it for you?
Discounted ING Health Insurance
An additional Rest Day to support your wellbeing
An IMPACT Day to volunteer on approved sustainability activity
About UsAt ING, we want to make life simpler and more worthwhile – for everyone who banks with us, for the people who work with us, and the community at large, too.When you come to work at ING, you’re joining a team where individuality isn’t just accepted, it’s encouraged. We’ve built a culture that’s fun, friendly and supportive – it’s the kind of place where you can be yourself and make the most of whatever you have to offer.We give people the freedom to think differently, take ownership of their work, and make great things happen. We’re here to help you get ahead. And with our global network, there’s plenty of scope to take your career in new directions, perhaps even ones you’ve never considered.We are all about celebrating success and as a result we are proud to be a WGEA Employer of Choice for Gender Equality and a certified Family Inclusive workplace.Sound like the kind of place you’d feel at home? We’d love to hear from you.(One last thing, ING operates a direct talent sourcing model. So no agency introductions, please.)
Need more?Contact Mark Montgomery onmark.montgomery@ing.com
